question.text: Once your vehicle is parked, where should it sit in relation to the travel lanes and other drivers?

answer.text: Once parked, your vehicle must not become a hazard, so leave it far enough from any travel lane that it does not get in the way and where drivers coming from either direction can see it.

teaching.text: A parked car becomes a hazard when it sits in a travel lane or where drivers cannot see it, so leave it clear and visible. Remember: out of the lane, in view.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Once parked, your vehicle must not become a hazard, so leave it far enough from any travel lane that it does not get in the way and where drivers coming from either direction can see it.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: out of the lane, in view

question.text: What kind of place should you choose for parking whenever you can?

answer.text: Use a designated parking area whenever you can.

teaching.text: Designated areas are built to keep parked cars out of traffic, which is why they are the first choice. Remember: designated spots first.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Use a designated parking area whenever you can.

question.text: If you have no choice but to park on the roadway itself, where should you place the vehicle?

answer.text: If you have to park on the roadway itself, get as far from traffic as you can, and pull as close as possible to the curb if there is one.

teaching.text: When there is no lot, tuck the car tight to the curb and as far from moving traffic as you can. Remember: hug the curb.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you have to park on the roadway itself, get as far from traffic as you can, and pull as close as possible to the curb if there is one.

question.text: What general rule about traffic and hazards decides whether a parking spot is allowed?

answer.text: Do not park where your vehicle blocks normal traffic or creates a hazard for other drivers.

teaching.text: This is the general test for any spot: if your car would block normal traffic or force others around a hazard, it is the wrong place. Remember: never block the flow.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Do not park where your vehicle blocks normal traffic or creates a hazard for other drivers.

question.text: What two things do you do every time you park, for the brake and for the transmission?

answer.text: Every time you park, set the parking brake, and leave a manual transmission in gear or an automatic in park.

teaching.text: The brake and the parked gear work together, and the guide asks for both every time, not only on hills. Remember: brake on, gear or park.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Every time you park, set the parking brake, and leave a manual transmission in gear or an automatic in park.

question.text: How does securing a parked manual car differ from securing an automatic?

answer.text: Leaving the transmission in gear applies to a manual car, while an automatic is left in park, and in both cases the parking brake is set.

teaching.text: A manual has no park position, so it stays in gear, while an automatic goes into park; the parking brake is set for both. Remember: manual gear, automatic park.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Leaving the transmission in gear applies to a manual car, while an automatic is left in park, and in both cases the parking brake is set.

question.text: What should you do with the keys and the doors when you leave a parked vehicle?

answer.text: Never leave the keys in a parked vehicle, and lock it any time it will be out of your sight.

teaching.text: Leaving keys inside invites theft, so the keys always come with you and the car is locked whenever you walk away from it. Remember: keys out, doors locked.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Never leave the keys in a parked vehicle, and lock it any time it will be out of your sight.

question.text: Before you open your door after parking, what do you check, and which side should you and your passengers get out on?

answer.text: Look for traffic before opening your door, get out on the curb side when possible, and have passengers, especially children, leave on the curb side too.

teaching.text: Children may not judge traffic well, so the curb side keeps them, and you, away from the travel lane. Remember: curb side out.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Look for traffic before opening your door, get out on the curb side when possible, and have passengers, especially children, leave on the curb side too.

question.text: Which road users should you watch for before opening a door next to the travel lane, and what do you do once you are out?

answer.text: Before opening a door, watch for cyclists, who often ride along the right edge of the travel lanes next to parked cars, and close the door as soon as you are out.

teaching.text: Cyclists often ride right beside parked cars, so a door opened without looking can strike a rider who has nowhere to go. Remember: look for bikes, shut fast.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Before opening a door, watch for cyclists, who often ride along the right edge of the travel lanes next to parked cars, and close the door as soon as you are out.

question.text: When may you open the street-side door after parking?

answer.text: Opening a door on the street side is allowed only after you check traffic first, since getting out on the curb side is preferred.

teaching.text: The curb side is the first choice, and the street-side door is still allowed once you have checked traffic. Remember: street door after a check.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Opening a door on the street side is allowed only after you check traffic first, since getting out on the curb side is preferred.

question.text: What two things must you do before pulling out of any parking space?

answer.text: Before pulling out of any parking space, check traffic and signal.

teaching.text: Checking and signaling before you move keeps drivers already in the lane from being surprised by a car pulling out. Remember: check, then signal.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Before pulling out of any parking space, check traffic and signal.

question.text: On a one-way street, which side of the street may you usually park on?

answer.text: On a one-way street you may usually park on either the left or the right side.

teaching.text: All traffic on a one-way street moves the same direction, which is why either side is usually open for parking. Remember: one-way, either side.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On a one-way street you may usually park on either the left or the right side.

question.text: On a two-way street, which side and which facing direction are forbidden for parking?

answer.text: Do not park on the left side of a two-way street or with your vehicle facing against the flow of traffic.

teaching.text: A car on the left side of a two-way street ends up facing oncoming traffic, which is exactly what the rule forbids. Remember: never left, never facing traffic.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Do not park on the left side of a two-way street or with your vehicle facing against the flow of traffic.

question.text: How does the street type change which side you may park on?

answer.text: Street side depends on the street type: a one-way street normally allows parking on either side, while a two-way street forbids parking on the left side.

teaching.text: Decide by street type first: one-way usually allows either side, two-way never the left. Remember: one-way either, two-way right.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Street side depends on the street type: a one-way street normally allows parking on either side, while a two-way street forbids parking on the left side.

question.text: Besides signs, what else can show you that parking is banned or limited?

answer.text: Look for signs that ban or limit parking, and note that some limits are shown by colored curb markings.

teaching.text: Look at both the sign posts and the curb paint, because either one can carry a parking limit. Remember: read the curb colors.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Look for signs that ban or limit parking, and note that some limits are shown by colored curb markings.

question.text: Which curb color, which structure and which piece of fire equipment mean no parking next to them?

answer.text: Parking is forbidden next to a curb painted yellow, on a bridge, or in front of a fire hydrant.

teaching.text: Yellow curbs, bridges and fire hydrants must stay clear, and hydrants especially need open access for emergency crews. Remember: yellow, bridge, hydrant.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Parking is forbidden next to a curb painted yellow, on a bridge, or in front of a fire hydrant.

question.text: Can a colored curb limit parking where no sign is posted, and what does a yellow curb mean?

answer.text: Colored curb markings can signal a parking limit even where no sign is posted, and a curb painted yellow means no parking there.

teaching.text: No sign does not mean parking is allowed; the paint on the curb can be the rule by itself. Remember: yellow paint, no parking.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Colored curb markings can signal a parking limit even where no sign is posted, and a curb painted yellow means no parking there.

question.text: Name the four places where you must never park, involving an intersection, pedestrians and a driveway.

answer.text: Never park inside an intersection, on a crosswalk or sidewalk, or across the entrance to a driveway.

teaching.text: These spots are where people walk or cross and where cars turn or enter, so a parked car there blocks them. Remember: corners, crossings, walks, driveways.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Never park inside an intersection, on a crosswalk or sidewalk, or across the entrance to a driveway.

question.text: What does the International Symbol of Access mark?

answer.text: The International Symbol of Access marks spaces reserved for vehicles driven by or carrying people with disabilities.

teaching.text: The symbol tells you the space is reserved for vehicles driven by or carrying people with disabilities. Remember: symbol means reserved.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The International Symbol of Access marks spaces reserved for vehicles driven by or carrying people with disabilities.

question.text: Which vehicles may use a handicapped space, and when?

answer.text: A handicapped space may be used only by a vehicle showing a disability placard or plates, and only while a person with a physical disability is in it or is being dropped off or picked up.

teaching.text: Both conditions must be true at once: the placard or plates are showing, and the person with a disability is there. Remember: placard plus passenger.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A handicapped space may be used only by a vehicle showing a disability placard or plates, and only while a person with a physical disability is in it or is being dropped off or picked up.

question.text: Is showing a disability placard or plates enough by itself to use a reserved space?

answer.text: Showing a disability placard or plates is not enough by itself; the reserved space also needs a person with a physical disability riding in the car or being dropped off or picked up.

teaching.text: Many drivers stop at the placard, but the person with a disability must be riding along or being dropped off or picked up. Remember: placard needs the person.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Showing a disability placard or plates is not enough by itself; the reserved space also needs a person with a physical disability riding in the car or being dropped off or picked up.

question.text: Is it legal to park in the striped access aisle beside a handicapped space?

answer.text: Parking in the striped access aisle beside a handicapped space is illegal.

teaching.text: The striped aisle gives room for wheelchairs, ramps and doors, so it must stay empty even though it looks like spare pavement. Remember: stripes stay empty.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Parking in the striped access aisle beside a handicapped space is illegal.

question.text: When is using another person's disability placard or plates to take a handicapped space illegal?

answer.text: Using someone's disability placard or plates to take a handicapped space is illegal when that person is not riding along at the time.

teaching.text: A borrowed placard only works when its holder is in the car; without that person, using the space is illegal. Remember: no holder, no space.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Using someone's disability placard or plates to take a handicapped space is illegal when that person is not riding along at the time.

question.text: What are the two separate offenses around reserved handicapped spaces?

answer.text: Two separate offenses apply around reserved spaces: parking in the access aisle, and using another person's placard or plates when that person is not being carried.

teaching.text: Keep the two offenses apart: one is about where you park, the aisle, and the other is about using someone's placard without them. Remember: aisle and borrowed placard.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Two separate offenses apply around reserved spaces: parking in the access aisle, and using another person's placard or plates when that person is not being carried.

question.text: What fine range applies to a conviction for misusing a handicapped space?

answer.text: A conviction for misusing a handicapped space brings a fine of at least fifty dollars and no more than three hundred dollars.

teaching.text: Remember the two ends of the range, fifty dollars at the low end and three hundred dollars at the high end. Remember: fifty up to three hundred.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A conviction for misusing a handicapped space brings a fine of at least fifty dollars and no more than three hundred dollars.

question.text: When you park on a hill, which way do you turn the front wheels?

answer.text: When parked on a hill, turn the wheels sharply toward the side of the road so that a rolling car moves away from traffic.

teaching.text: The turned wheels are a backup: if the brake slips, they steer the car toward the roadside instead of into the lane. Remember: wheels to the roadside.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When parked on a hill, turn the wheels sharply toward the side of the road so that a rolling car moves away from traffic.

question.text: Why do you turn the wheels toward the roadside when parking on a hill?

answer.text: The reason for turning the wheels toward the roadside on a hill is so the car rolls away from traffic if it starts to move.

teaching.text: The whole point of the wheel turn is where a rolling car would go, and the answer is away from traffic. Remember: roll away from traffic.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The reason for turning the wheels toward the roadside on a hill is so the car rolls away from traffic if it starts to move.

question.text: Before leaving a car parked on a hill, what do you do with the wheels, the engine and gear, and the brake?

answer.text: Before leaving a car parked on a hill, turn the wheels the proper way, shut off the engine with the vehicle in the proper gear, and set the parking or emergency brake.

teaching.text: Each step adds a layer: the wheels choose the direction, the gear backs up the brake, and the brake holds the car. Remember: wheels, engine, brake.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Before leaving a car parked on a hill, turn the wheels the proper way, shut off the engine with the vehicle in the proper gear, and set the parking or emergency brake.

question.text: On the hill checklist, what is the emergency brake?

answer.text: The hill checklist on this page uses the words emergency or parking brake for the same brake that must be set on any parked vehicle.

teaching.text: There is no extra brake to find on a hill; emergency brake and parking brake name the same one. Remember: emergency equals parking brake.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The hill checklist on this page uses the words emergency or parking brake for the same brake that must be set on any parked vehicle.

question.text: What are the last steps of leaving a car parked on a hill, from the keys to locking up?

answer.text: To finish leaving a car parked on a hill, take the keys out, check the rearview mirror for traffic before stepping out, then lock the car and keep the keys with you.

teaching.text: You will be opening a door next to the lane, so the mirror check comes before you step out, and the keys go with you. Remember: keys, mirror, lock.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To finish leaving a car parked on a hill, take the keys out, check the rearview mirror for traffic before stepping out, then lock the car and keep the keys with you.

question.text: How does parking on a hill end, in terms of the key and the car?

answer.text: Parking on hills ends with the same security habit as any other stop: take the key out of the ignition, lock up, and keep the keys with you.

teaching.text: The hill routine ends the same way as any stop, with the key out, the car locked and the keys in your pocket. Remember: key out, lock, keep keys.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Parking on hills ends with the same security habit as any other stop: take the key out of the ignition, lock up, and keep the keys with you.

question.text: Where do you stop to begin parallel parking?

answer.text: To begin parallel parking, stop alongside the car in front of the empty space, about one and a half feet to its left.

teaching.text: Starting beside the car ahead gives you the angle you need to back into the space without scraping it. Remember: beside the car ahead.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To begin parallel parking, stop alongside the car in front of the empty space, about one and a half feet to its left.

question.text: After the starting stop, how do you turn the wheels and move into the parallel space, and what must your front end avoid?

answer.text: Next, turn the wheels sharply right and back slowly into the space, making sure your front end does not block passing or oncoming traffic.

teaching.text: Back in slowly, because the front of your car swings out toward the street as the rear moves toward the curb. Remember: sharp right, back slow.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Next, turn the wheels sharply right and back slowly into the space, making sure your front end does not block passing or oncoming traffic.

question.text: Once your front end clears the car ahead, what wheel turns finish the parallel park, and where should you end?

answer.text: Once your front clears the car ahead, turn the wheels sharply left and keep backing, then turn sharply right and pull forward toward the curb, ending in the middle of the space.

teaching.text: The sharp left straightens the car once the front is clear, and the final sharp right brings it in line with the curb. Remember: left, then right, centered.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Once your front clears the car ahead, turn the wheels sharply left and keep backing, then turn sharply right and pull forward toward the curb, ending in the middle of the space.

question.text: In parallel parking, what is the order of the sharp wheel turns?

answer.text: In parallel parking the wheel turns run sharp right, then sharp left, then sharp right again as you pull toward the curb.

teaching.text: Say the order to yourself while you practice: right as you back in, left once clear, right as you pull forward. Remember: right, left, right.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In parallel parking the wheel turns run sharp right, then sharp left, then sharp right again as you pull toward the curb.

question.text: Where should your car end up at the finish of a parallel park?

answer.text: During parallel parking the final position is the center of the space, not pressed against the car ahead or behind.

teaching.text: Ending in the center leaves room on both ends so the cars ahead and behind can pull out later. Remember: middle of the space.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: During parallel parking the final position is the center of the space, not pressed against the car ahead or behind.
